Usage: astryx integration check [options]

The CI check for an integration package's own build: every source check, run in continuous integration or a typecheck script, against the package in the current folder

Options:
  --strict    Also exit 1 on any warning and on any check that did not run. A new check or failure code joins only in a minor release, named in the release notes; until then, a malformed `cliCommand` is reported as a note (`invalid_cli_command`) that fails nothing.
  --next      Also count the findings the next minor release turns into warnings (the notes marked `next`) as warnings now, so `--strict --next` fails on them. Run it to fix them ahead of the release; every run says how many there are.
  -h, --help  display help for command

Exit codes:
  0  no check fails on its own; with --strict, also no warning, and every check ran
  1  a check fails on its own (an error); with --strict, also any warning, or a check that did not run

Examples:
  # In CI, as the typecheck script: add "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit && astryx integration check --strict" to package.json
  npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration check --strict
  # Errors only, while you fix the warnings a package already has
  npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration check
  # Fix ahead: fail on the findings the next minor release will fail on
  npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration check --strict --next
  # Read the result as JSON
  npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration check --strict --json
  # Before you publish: check that the packed package works in an app
  npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 integration verify

More: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs cli/commands/integration-check
